newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower amid projections for continued light packer demand, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
A number of Midwest pork plants reduced output Monday in attempts to turn operating margins positive, company and trade sources said.

Reductions at the various companies' plants were estimated at one to two hours per shift on a day-to-day basis, sources said. Margins were squeezed by higher cash hog prices last week and soft pork demand which weighed on wholesale prices.

Pork prices at midday were mixed, with hams weighing 17-20 lbs steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, 20-26 lb hams steady to $1.00 lower and pork bellies not fully established, USDA said. There were 13.0 loads of pork cuts and 8.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold, USDA's central carlot report said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plant were ranging from $56.50 to $57.00, sources there said.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range $56.00 to $56.50. Top prices for Indiana/Ohio hogs at the plant could span $55.75 to $56.25, sources in those areas said.
